title: Top-down and middle-down proteomic analysis of Shiga toxin using MALDI-TOF-TOF mass spectrometry
author: Fagerquist, Zaragoza

However, the supernatant may be filter sterilized with a 0.2 μm filter as an extra precaution.10Sample and matrix spotting/drying can produce variable results at times due to laboratory humidity and other factors. In consequence, a minimum of five spots (five technical replicates) per sample should be performed.11For analysis of the disulfide bond-reduced B-subunit (linear chain secondary structure), 0.5 μL of 1 M dithiothreitol (DTT, Sigma-Aldrich) is added to 30 μL of supernatant and is heated in a water bath at 70 °C for 10 min in an Eppendorf tube. A 0.6 μL aliquot of this solution is spotted directly onto the stainless steel MALDI target plate and allowed to dry. The dried sample spot is then overlayed with a 0.6 μL aliquot of saturated solution of sinapinic acid MALDI matrix which is also allowed to dry.12For analysis of both the A2 fragment of the A-subunit and the disulfide bond-reduced B-subunit, 0.5 μL of furin (New England Biolabs, MA) is added to 30 μL of supernatant in an Eppendorf tube, incubated at 37 °C for 45 min after which 0.5 μL of DTT is added to the tube and the solution is heated in a water bath at 70 °C for 10 min. A 0.6 μL aliquot of this solution is spotted directly onto the stainless steel MALDI target plate and allowed to dry.13Caveat: Furin is shipped by the vendor on dry ice and in a solution that contains glycerol so that it remains cold but does not freeze and damage the enzymatic activity of the furin. However, glycerol is viscous compound and does not evaporate readily at room temperature. The glycerol present in the furin-treated sample will not dry completely (or at all) when spotted onto the MALDI target. After spotting, allow 15 min for the spot to “dry”.14The “dried” furin-treated sample spot is then overlayed with a 0.6 μL aliquot of saturated solution of sinapinic acid MALDI matrix which is also allowed to dry (and gives the appearance of drying).

steps.title: Work in BSL‑2 cabinet
steps.instruction: Perform all manipulations of STEC in a Class‑2 Biohazard safety cabinet (BSL‑2).

steps.title: Overnight culture on LBA with antibiotic
steps.instruction: Streak STEC onto Luria‑Bertani agar (LBA) supplemented with the chosen antibiotic and incubate overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Screen antibiotic concentrations for toxin induction
steps.instruction: Prepare parallel cultures with ciprofloxacin at 10 ng mL⁻¹ and 20 ng mL⁻¹, mitomycin‑C at 800 ng mL⁻¹ and 1200 ng mL⁻¹, and a no‑antibiotic control; incubate overnight to assess Shiga toxin expression.

steps.title: Detect toxin by linear‑mode MS
steps.instruction: Analyze each culture in linear‑mode MALDI‑TOF MS, monitoring the disulfide‑bond‑intact B‑subunit mass to identify the optimal antibiotic condition.

steps.title: Harvest cells with flush loop
steps.instruction: Using a flush 1 µL inoculating loop (filled to the depth of the loop), collect cells and transfer into a sterile screw‑cap microcentrifuge tube containing 300 µL sterile water (Fisher Chemical).

steps.title: Disperse cells without lysis
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube for less than 15 seconds to disperse cellular and extracellular material while avoiding extensive cell lysis.

steps.title: Pellet cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 13,000 rpm for 5 minutes; keep the supernatant for downstream processing.

steps.title: Optional filter‑sterilize supernatant
steps.instruction: Pass the supernatant through a 0.2 µm syringe filter as an extra precaution.

steps.title: Spot intact B‑subunit and apply matrix
steps.instruction: In the BSL‑2 cabinet, pipette 0.6 µL of the supernatant onto a 384‑spot stainless‑steel MALDI target plate and allow to air‑dry. Immediately overlay with 0.6 µL of freshly prepared saturated sinapinic acid matrix (33 % acetonitrile, 67 % water, 0.1 % trifluoroacetic acid) and let dry. Perform at least five technical replicate spots per sample.
